title: Windowed hedging + kernel-probe policy for gradual phase-splitting with tenant-priority fairness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: latency-sensitive tenants sometimes starve when we aggressively consolidate prefill/decode phases to maximize throughput. We need a policy that balances latency and throughput by doing gradual phase splits, opportunistic hedging, and light-weight kernel probing so kernel selection cost is considered in scheduling decisions. This ticket defines the windowed-hedging + kernel-probe scheduling policy, instrumentation, and rollout plan.
background: Recent runtime experiments showed that large-scale phase coalescing yields higher overall GPU utilization but increases  tail latency for low-SLO tenants when microbursts collide. Kernel selection can change execution time by ~15-30% for certain model/len pairs; without awareness the scheduler picks splits that are suboptimal for latency. Previous tickets focused on static heuristics and global fairshare; this work combines time-windowed hedging with lightweight kernel probes to make split decisions tenant-aware and latency-sensitive.
proposed_solution: Introduce a windowed hedging controller that maintains per-tenant latency headroom budgets and a small sliding window of recent kernel latency probes for common model archetypes. When a prefill is eligible for phase split, the controller evaluates: 1) tenant headroom (remaining ms budget), 2) probe-informed estimated kernel latency delta for split vs merged phase, and 3) global throughput score. If headroom is low, prefer conservative split (preserve latency). If probe indicates split is fast on current kernel, allow more aggressive consolidation. Hedging: for uncertain cases, duplicate a small fraction of requests (hedged clone path) to measure real-time kernel/path latency for future decisions. Ensure hedged clones are rate-limited and do not double-bill customers. Kernel probes are constant-time micro-executions (short memory-priming ops) recorded to a lightweight histogram indexed by (model-family, seq-bin, device-type).
implementation_steps:
1) Add kernel-probe microtask: define probe op, sampling rate, and histograms.
2) Extend tenant scheduler state with sliding headroom budget and penalty decay.
3) Implement windowed-hedging controller in arbiter: scoring function combining headroom, probe delta, and throughput weight.
4) Add hedged clone plumbing with throttles and billing-safe flags.
5) Expose runtime toggles and per-tenant weights via Console and config API.
6) Add metrics and tracing (per-tenant latency, hedged clone ratio, kernel probe histograms, split decisions).
7) End-to-end tests and canary rollout to non-critical region.
tradeoffs: Pros: adaptive to real kernel behavior, provides latency protection for high-SLO tenants, better-informed split choices. Cons: additional micro-probes add small overhead and complexity, hedged clones increase load and must be tightly controlled, more moving pieces for debugging. There's also a risk of oscillation if scores are noisy; use smoothing and conservative defaults.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Kernel probe histograms ingest and persist with <=2s latency and <0.1% increase in tail GPU occupancy.
2) Windowed hedging controller makes consistent split decisions (agreement metric) vs baseline in >=90% of low-latency scenarios where headroom is available.
3) For a mixed-tenant test harness, 95th percentile latency for P0 tenants improves or stays within 5% of baseline while throughput loss is <=7%.
4) Hedged clone ratio defaults to 0.5% of traffic and can be toggled per-tenant.
5) No customer is double-billed for hedged clones; billing flags respected end-to-end.
6) Console shows per-tenant headroom and probe histograms in runtime observability dashboards.
metrics_and_monitoring: Key metrics: tenant_headroom_ms, probe_latency_p50/p95, split_decision_count(by reason), hedged_clone_rate, hedged_clone_success_delta, kernel_probe_error_rate, downstream_queue_wait. Set alerts: avg_headroom < 10ms for P0 tenants (S1), hedged_clone_rate > configured cap (S2), probe_error_rate >1% (S2).
test_plan: Unit tests for probe sampling and histogram; integration tests with simulated kernels (fast/slow) to validate decision surface; chaos test to ensure hedged clones controlled under burst; load test comparing latency/throughput tradeoffs across multiple tenant mixes; canary rollout to us-west-2 with 5% of traffic, monitor for 48h before expanding.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: feature flag off in prod, enable probe-only mode (collection) in limited regions.
Phase 2: enable controller in read-only simulation mode (decisions logged).
Phase 3: enable hedging at 0.5% traffic and per-tenant opt-in for P0s, monitor 48h.
Phase 4: increase coverage to 25% of tenants and tune weights.
Phase 5: global rollout with operator dashboard.
manual_mitigation: If tail latency regresses: disable hedging, revert controller to conservative fixed-split policy, roll back probe sampling. If probe infra causes errors: disable probe ingestion pipeline and fall back to historical kernel estimates.
notes: Design reviewed with SRE and PM on 2026-03-09. Data from model-catalog suggests LLaMA-family variants have the highest variance across kernels; prioritize those for probes. Billing and legal reviewed hedged clone policy for customer safety. Need follow-up to update SDK docs.
